title: Critical-lattice phase extraction, blockwise occupancy, and finite-section control

sibling_isolation.reason: The sibling attempt has a separate live lease and is not an input to this run.

claims.statement: For a connected weighted graph with Poincare constant lambda_G and edge coordinate radius R, some phase tau satisfies sum_i w_i dist_T(x_i-tau,Z)^2 <= pi^2 R^2 E_sinc/(2 lambda_G).
For complete block weights a_ij=w_i w_j, the exact weighted graph gap is sum_i w_i, so bounded-block sinc energy directly controls distance to one local lattice phase.

If a positive-integer-weighted real configuration has total ideal long-scale sinc energy E=eN, then for every fixed local radius r there is a shifted block partition deleting at most [(pi^2/2)R^2 e/eta^2+2r/R]N mass so every retained r-neighborhood lies eta-close to one blockwise lattice translate. Choosing R=e^(-1/5), eta=e^(1/5) gives O_r(e^(1/5)) deletion and error.
An overlap of mass Q with phase errors E_tau and E_sigma obeys Q dist_T(tau-sigma,Z)^2 <= 2(E_tau+E_sigma); a connected block graph gives the stated global weighted phase bound.

In the periodized ideal model, block phases and local block densities may vary: nonnegative cross-block deletion plus Cauchy recovers s1/N >= 2-1/theta-alpha theta/(3 omega_alpha)-epsilon/omega_alpha.
For a finite sinc-squared Toeplitz block, the missing-row-sum expansion yields an exact lower bound with boundary quantities B_d and C_d, with explicit B_d=O(log d) and C_d=O(1) estimates.
At relative scale alpha=3/4, points displaced by at most eta<=1/4 from assigned lattice cells change the short sinc-squared quadratic form by at most 25.226 eta times the cell second moment.
Two disconnected integer cosets have zero local edge sinc energy but positive best common-phase loss, so connectedness, overlap, or block locality is necessary.
The path x_j=j+j/n has sinc energy Theta(1/n), graph gap Theta(1/n^2), and common-phase loss Theta(n), showing that inverse-gap dependence is necessary in a global graph argument.

validation.result: PASS for local synchronization, complete blocks, overlap stitching, finite-Toeplitz correction, approximate-cell kernel stability, random-partition extraction, disconnected cosets and low-gap path scaling
validation.boundary: Deterministic checks validate finite formulas and implementations only; they do not prove any Zeta23 analytic input.

next_frontier: Derive effective on-line complete sinc/taper energy o(N) from near equality of the full indefinite Zeta23 P+Q certificate, or construct an admissible countermodel satisfying complete-frame pair inertia and finite-section constraints. Then combine the extraction, Toeplitz and kernel-stability losses with the A-RH-RTD-0002 fixed-theta budget.
cannot_imply: The parent attempts remain pending independent verification.
The long-scale on-line energy E=o(N) is an unresolved Zeta23 implication, not an assumption proved here.
The blockwise ideal theorem does not by itself control the smooth taper, finite grid, off-line pairs, tails or normalization.
The 25.226 coefficient is a coarse valid finite bound, not an optimized constant and not a zeta theorem.
No unconditional zeta-zero proportion has been improved.
This attempt does not prove or refute the Riemann hypothesis.
No claim is repository-verified before a fresh isolated verifier returns PASS on frozen artifact hashes.
